aidb_assessment.novelty: High at the evaluation-and-systems boundary: the central contribution is not a new storage primitive, but an auditable combination of temporal entries, source precedence, explicit deletion, evidence-level scoring, and scrubbed episodic fallback.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The controlled evidence-level results, held-out seeds, cost accounting, and explicit failure taxonomy justify close study and replication. Adoption would be premature because the strongest advantage comes from a co-designed synthetic workload, deletion guarantees are conditional and incomplete across storage surfaces, and no downstream-agent benefit has been demonstrated.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: Potentially high for agent systems where facts change and privacy-sensitive deletion matters. Fallback is the most defensible configuration for conflicting facts; augment is better suited to one-off conversational details but transfers correctness responsibility back to the answer model.

executive_summary: LEDGER separates fallible language-model extraction and routing from deterministic rules for supersession, source trust, temporal validity, and deletion; LEDGER+EP optionally retrieves scrubbed raw turns. Its strongest evidence is on an author-built synthetic coding workload: fallback substantially improves answer accuracy over full replay while exposing far fewer forbidden values and no deleted values in evaluated description-only deletion probes. Held-out seeds preserve but reduce the advantage. On LongMemEval, augment matches full replay’s observed accuracy with much less context, but confidence intervals do not establish equivalence or superiority. The design is promising for auditable memory, yet downstream agent utility, real-world deletion safety, delayed facts, broader models, and independent workloads remain unvalidated.

assumptions: Extraction must produce the correct value and stable slot key and must avoid claims from questions, plans, or negations.
Routing must find every relevant slot and no irrelevant slot; a missed deletion slot is a privacy failure.
The configured source ranking must reflect actual reliability.
Valid time begins when a value is stated; dates expressed inside text are not interpreted.
The caller must supply the correct user identifier and all reads and deletions must use the partitioned interface.
key_components: Per-user entity/attribute slots containing value entries with validity intervals and event provenance.
Five deterministic ingestion rules for restatement, trusted supersession, lower-trust disputes, trusted introduction, and unconfirmed low-trust claims.
Lexical grounding and enumerated-event safeguards applied before ledger writes.
Question and deletion routing over known slots, with explicit abstention reasons.
A scrubbed raw-turn episode store using BM25 retrieval in fallback or augment mode.
Evidence-level scoring that separately labels stale, future, contaminated, resurrected, and deleted values.
method.overview: A language-model extractor converts session events into slot-value claims and a router maps questions or deletion descriptions to known slots. A deterministic ledger core applies source-precedence, supersession, temporal-history, deduplication, abstention, and deletion rules. Each entry records validity, source kind, trust, and provenance. LEDGER+EP adds a BM25 episode store: fallback searches raw turns only when the ledger returns no fact, whereas augment always fills remaining context with turns. Deletion erases ledger records, retains value-free tombstones, blocks source events, and scrubs related episode turns.

open_questions: Can source trust be learned or configured per domain while remaining auditable and resistant to manipulation?
How should valid and recording time be separated when users report changes retrospectively?
Can deletion be made end-to-end across snapshots, caches, logs, embeddings, backups, and provider requests?
Does cleaner evidence improve success and safety on real multi-session coding tasks rather than checkpoint question answering?
Which component causes the gain: deterministic rules, extraction quality, routing, episode retrieval, scrubbing, or their interaction?

problem.importance: Answer-only evaluation can conceal unsafe evidence: a model may select the right answer from stale or conflicting context, while deleted information has still been disclosed to the answering provider.
problem.scope: The paper studies single-current-value facts in English coding-agent sessions and LongMemEval chats. It evaluates evidence packets and question answers, not an agent completing downstream software-engineering tasks.
problem.statement: Persistent agent memories must decide which changing fact is current, resolve conflicts between sources of unequal reliability, answer historical questions, abstain when evidence is absent, and honor deletion without resurfacing erased values.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Full replay and transcript RAG using the same agent, model, tools, task budget, and repositories.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: On real multi-session repository work, deterministic ledger evidence improves downstream task success and reduces regressions caused by stale configuration facts.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Blindly graded downstream task success, paired with the rate of actions attributable to stale, conflicting, or deleted evidence.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after the preregistered task set is complete, or earlier if a safety rule is violated; reject the hypothesis if the paired confidence interval does not exclude no improvement.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Current LEDGER+EP deletion pipeline, compared with a stricter semantic scrubber and storage-wide deletion across snapshots, caches, logs, and indexes.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: End-to-end deletion testing with adversarial paraphrases will reveal exposure paths not covered by slot routing and lexical episode scrubbing.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Deleted-value exposure rate across evidence, restored state, caches, logs, and answer outputs, plus retained-answer accuracy on unrelated facts.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop when the preregistered adversarial suite is exhausted; require zero observed exposure and a predefined bound on unrelated recall loss before considering the stronger pipeline acceptable.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The final fallback configuration with extraction, routing, trust rules, episodic retrieval, scrubbing, and token budget independently removed or replaced.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Factorial ablation will show that deterministic conflict and temporal rules, rather than co-varying extraction changes, account for most of the coding-workload advantage.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Held-out evidence accuracy and answer accuracy, supplemented by stale, contaminated, deleted, and false-abstention rates.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after all preregistered component combinations and independent workload seeds are evaluated; reject the hypothesis if rule removal does not cause the largest reproducible degradation.
